name: Light Color Temperature as Temporal and Ecological Prediction Signal
short_description: CCT serves as temporal and ecological prediction signal; congruence produces fluency, violation produces PE with circadian, cognitive, and affective consequences
structural_pattern: The correlated color temperature (CCT) of ambient light serves as both a temporal prediction signal and an ecological prediction signal. The brain maintains expectations about light color based on time of day (warm/low-CCT light predicts morning, evening, or firelight; cool/high-CCT light predicts midday or overcast conditions) and ecological context (warm light predicts interior/intimate/safe; cool light predicts exterior/open/exposed). When architectural lighting CCT matches the temporal and ecological context, predictions are confirmed, processing is fluent, and the affective response is congruent. When CCT violates context (blue-white 6500K light in an evening residential space; dim warm 2700K light during morning work hours), the result is temporal-ecological PE that manifests as discomfort, incongruity, or circadian disruption. Additionally, CCT modulates arousal and processing style: cool/bright light → precision-weighted processing (analytical, detail-focused); warm/dim light → relaxed prediction weighting (creative, relational).
higher_order_principle: Cross-modal prediction congruence (AX5) applied to the temporal and ecological dimensions of light. CCT is a prediction cue that the brain uses to infer time, context, and appropriate behavioral mode. Congruence = fluency; violation = PE with downstream circadian, cognitive, and affective consequences.

causal_links.evidence_base: CCT implicitly communicates time of day. ~2000-3000K = sunrise/sunset/firelight (evening, rest). ~5000-6500K = midday/overcast (alertness, activity). Violation (cool light at night) produces temporal incongruity.

Not merely symbolic: blue-enriched (high-CCT) light at evening directly suppresses melatonin onset via L2 pathway. The circadian system responds to spectral content, not perceived color warmth. Temporal incongruity is both psychologically uncomfortable and physiologically disruptive.

Cool/bright → heightened arousal → narrower prediction intervals → analytical processing (Steidle & Werth, 2013; Feldman & Friston, 2010 precision weighting). Warm/dim → lowered arousal → wider prediction intervals → creative/relational processing.

Surfaces are expected to appear under daylight-like spectra (Hurlbert, 2007). Extreme CCT departures distort surface colors beyond color constancy range → chromatic PE (Conway, 2009). Used deliberately by Turrell and theatrical lighting designers for perceptual transformation effects.

scope_conditions: Strongest effects when CCT is clearly incongruent with temporal or social context
Tunable/dynamic CCT systems can match natural daylight variation and minimize temporal PE
Cultural modulation: warm-light preference is near-universal but the exact preferred CCT varies by culture and context
moderators: Illuminance level: CCT effects interact with brightness (warm dim light is cozy; warm bright light is unusual)
Context expectations: a restaurant at 2700K is expected; a hospital operating room at 2700K violates expectations
Time of day: same CCT has different effects depending on circadian phase

interactions.nature: L4 specifies the spectral/CCT dimension that feeds into L2's circadian entrainment pathway. CCT is the perceptually accessible proxy for the melanopic content that L2 operates on.
L4 is a specific instance of cross-modal prediction congruence: visual CCT cue predicts temporal context; congruence = fluency; violation = PE.
L1 operates on luminance distribution (light-dark); L4 operates on chromaticity (warm-cool). Independent channels that jointly determine the visual character of architectural light.

maturity_note: Ecological and arousal interpretations not yet empirically distinguished. Core CCT-mood and CCT-cognition findings replicated but with inconsistencies.

dual_interpretation.reasoning: Ecological-signal framing integrates naturally with PE framework and generates testable predictions that arousal account does not

ecological_signal_account.mechanism: Brain uses CCT as ecological TIME-OF-DAY signal triggering corresponding processing modes
evidence_for: Dim/warm → creativity effect replicated in multiple laboratories
Effect operates through construal level (dim light promotes abstract, high-level construal)
Effect interacts with light COLOR, not just intensity — warm CCT at moderate illuminance promotes creativity more than cool CCT
ecological_signal_account.key_prediction: Cool light at low illuminance is ecologically incongruent → should produce DISCOMFORT or cognitive interference

arousal_mediation_account.mechanism: CCT → arousal → processing mode (simple mediation without ecological prediction)
evidence_for: Replication landscape uneven — variable effect sizes and published failures to replicate
Cool bright light is more arousing than warm dim light; arousal modulates processing style
Studies controlling illuminance while varying CCT alone generally find smaller or null effects
arousal_mediation_account.key_objection: Color constancy mechanisms compensate for illuminant changes — if system discounts CCT, cannot simultaneously use it as ecological signal

critical_experiment_to_resolve.design: Congruent (6500K morning → 3000K evening) vs Incongruent (3000K morning → 6500K evening) vs Constant (4500K throughout)
critical_experiment_to_resolve.ecological_prediction: Incongruent WORSE than constant (active violation > absence)
critical_experiment_to_resolve.arousal_prediction: Incongruent and constant equivalent (both lack arousal-modulation benefit)

calibration_parameters.evaluation_guidance: Article Eater should evaluate CCT-cognition findings against BOTH interpretations and note which aspects of study design favor one account over the other
calibration_parameters.calibration_source: Panel L-II (Doc 49) — Steidle-Veitch debate and panel verdict
